title: Heartstopper Forever Gives Netflix's Beloved Queer Romance a Bittersweet Farewell
excerpt: Alice Oseman's feature-length finale trades fairy-tale warmth for a mature, emotionally honest goodbye to Charlie and Nick — and earns a 95 percent Rotten Tomatoes score in the process.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Heartstopper Forever, a 111-minute film, debuts on Netflix on July 17, 2026.
  • Stars Kit Connor and Joe Locke return as Nick and Charlie, now as executive producers.
  • The film addresses mature themes like long-distance anxiety and jealousy, diverging from the show's lighter tone.
  • Heartstopper Forever holds a 95% Rotten Tomatoes score, praised for performances but criticized for compressed storytelling.

  • Heartstopper Forever, a 111-minute film directed by Wash Westmoreland, debuts on Netflix on July 17, 2026, replacing a planned fourth season as the franchise's conclusion.
  • Stars Kit Connor and Joe Locke return as Nick and Charlie while also serving as executive producers for the first time, with Anna Maxwell Martin stepping in for Olivia Colman as Nick's mother.
  • The film tackles long-distance anxiety, alcohol use, and jealousy as the couple faces university separation — a deliberate pivot from the show's lighter early tone.
  • Critics have praised the finale, which holds a 95 percent Rotten Tomatoes score, though some note the compressed format shortchanges the ensemble cast.

A Feature Film Instead of a Final Season

When Netflix greenlit Heartstopper in 2022, few predicted the British teen romance would become one of the platform's most culturally significant properties. Adapted from Alice Oseman's graphic novels, the show logged 53.46 million hours viewed in its first three weeks and sustained that momentum across three seasons. Yet the finale arrives not as a season but as a feature film — a shift reportedly driven by viewing figures and contractual obligations that made a full eight-episode run untenable.

The result is Heartstopper Forever, a 111-minute movie directed by Wash Westmoreland, best known for co-directing Still Alice. Oseman wrote the screenplay, and the film premiered at a London event on July 15 before streaming globally on July 17.

Growing Pains for Charlie and Nick

Set during the characters' final year at Truham Grammar School, the film centres on a question every young couple dreads: can we survive being apart? Nick, now 18, is preparing for university, while Charlie — still processing his time in a mental health clinic — is finding his footing as a candidate for Head Boy.

The story leans into territory the series only hinted at. Nick turns to alcohol as he wrestles with the prospect of leaving Charlie behind. Charlie, meanwhile, battles jealousy. The animated hearts and fireworks that became the show's visual signature are still present, but dialled down, matching a narrative that asks harder questions about codependency and identity.

"Heartstopper starts like a fairy tale and a bit idealistic, in a beautiful way that we all love. But in the film, we're taking a slightly grittier look at romance and what it is to be in a long-term relationship."

- Alice Oseman, creator and writer

Stronger Performances, Compressed Arcs

Critics have largely praised the film, which holds a 95 percent score on Rotten Tomatoes against a 94 percent audience rating. Screen Rant called Joe Locke's performance "the strongest of his career thus far, with a turn that feels both sincere and vulnerable." Kit Connor draws particular notice for portraying Nick's brief downward spiral, especially in scenes opposite Anna Maxwell Martin, who replaces Olivia Colman as Nick's mother Sarah.

The compressed format, however, leaves scars. At roughly three-and-a-half episode equivalents, the film pushes most of the ensemble — Elle (Yasmin Finney), Tao (William Gao), Isaac (Tobie Donovan), Tara (Corinna Brown), Darcy (Kizzy Edgell) — to the periphery. A subplot about Elle speaking on her experiences as a Black trans girl is introduced but barely explored. The A.V. Club noted that "an entire season would've had the time to dig deeper into the subject matter."

A Franchise That Mattered — and Knows It

Connor and Locke, who served as executive producers for the first time, acknowledged the weight of the farewell. "As EPs, it feels like we can really say goodbye to them in a way that feels the most right," Connor told Netflix's Tudum. "It is bittersweet, but it is also a really nice way of ending it."

"As an actor, you can frankly not expect any of the jobs that you do to have the kind of impact that this show and this film hopefully will have. I feel very lucky for it every day."

- Kit Connor, actor and executive producer

Oseman, who released the sixth and final graphic novel volume earlier this month, told Reuters she would "never say never" to a spinoff but emphasised the deliberate closure. "I was really just doing this on the side as a fun side project, and now it's so important to so many people and I really don't take that lightly," she said.

Why It Resonates Beyond the UK

Heartstopper's global reach has always extended well past its British school setting. For diaspora audiences — including South Asian viewers who followed the show's frank treatment of coming out in conservative family structures — the series offered a rare model of queer adolescence where acceptance, though hard-won, was ultimately achievable. The film's exploration of long-distance love and the transition to adulthood mirrors an experience common among immigrant families navigating education systems far from home.

All three seasons and Heartstopper Forever are now streaming on Netflix.
